outcome: Fecal microbiota composition (phylogenetic profiles, relative abundance of various taxa like Bifidobacterium, Enterobacter, Enterococcus, Clostridium, Collinsella, Coprococcus, Lactobacillus)
cohort: Infants delivered by C-section (n=21) and vaginally (n=19) who received either a control formula or a formula containing L. reuteri within 72 hours of birth.
finding: A formula containing L. reuteri DSM 17938 does not significantly alter the microbiota in vaginally born infants, but in C-section-delivered infants, it appears to modulate early microbiota development towards a composition similar to that found after vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: The formula containing L. reuteri DSM 17938 did not essentially alter microbiota in vaginally born infants, but in C-section-delivered infants, it modulated the early microbiota toward the composition found after vaginal delivery.
